Kriyāsāra
------------------------------------------
This is a work of the tantra group dealing with the construction of temples as also the rituals, including the consecration of the इदोल्स्. Ravi, the son of सुब्रह्मण्य (belonging to Kerala) is the author of this work. It was probably composed during the 10th century A. D.
The work is spread over 69 paṭalas or sections and is in the śloka metre, the total number of verses being 3498.
The author seems to have been guided by the Vātulāgama while composing his work.
The work deals with the following deities: विष्णु; शिव; Harīśa or शङ्कर-नारायण; दुर्गा; स्कन्द; गणपति and शास्ता.
The various steps involved in the construction of a temple and consecration of the image are common to all these deities.
The more important ones are as follows: guruvaraṇa (choosing the chief priest); bhūparīkṣā (testing the soil); laying of the prathama-iṣṭikās (first bricks); rākṣoghnahoma (homa for driving away the evil spirits); Vāstuyāga (sacrifice to please the Vāstu-पुरुष or the deity of the site); ṣaḍādhāra pratiṣṭhā (See ṢAḌĀDHĀRAPRATIṢṬHĀ); rites of purification of the idol; aṣṭabandha and pratiṣṭhā (fixing the image with the special paste and consecration of the image); prāyaścittahoma (expiatory rites to offset the effects of procedural mistakes); pūjās and utsavas (worship of the deity and celebration of special days); dānas (giving gifts to participants and poor people); honouring the chief priest.
Towards the end, details about the construction of gośālā (cow-shed) with an image of कृष्ण as Govinda (protector of cows) and the temple or temples for the Mātṛkās (Saptamātṛkās or the seven goddesses) are also given.

Kriyāyogasāra
------------------------------------------
Purāṇas and उपपुराणस् have done yeoman service in spreading मोरलित्य् and religion among the masses.
The Bṛhad-धर्म-purāṇa (1.25) gives a list of उपपुराणस् in which Kriyāyogasāra is also one. It is a Vaiṣṇava work composed by someone in Bengal, probably in the 13th or the 14th century A. D.
Its teachings can be summarised as follows:
Kṛṣṇa is विष्णु himself. The Bhāgavatapurāṇa has to be studied well to understand him. Dāsyabhakti, the attitude of a servant towards the master, is the best for an ordinary sādhaka. Another discipline useful to the sādhaka is क्रियायोग. It means योग through kriyā or work. This can take the form of worshipping the गङ्गा, विष्णु and लक्ष्मी, showing respect to the ब्राह्मणस्, giving gifts to worthy and needy persons, observing एकादशी as a religious ritual with ड़स्तिन्ग् and worship, होस्पितलित्य् to guests and honouring the तुलसी plant.
This work seems to be a distinct and independent work confined to Bengal and throws some light on the contemporary society.

Kriyāyoga
(‘Yoga or union through kriyā or activity’)
------------------------------------------
This is a technical term used in the Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) (vide 2.1).
Yoga is conquering the modifications of मिन्द्, ultimately resulting in समाधि (perfect concentration, superconscious experience).
Patañjali recommends क्रियायोग for the benefit of ordinary sādhakas, who are incapable of practising all the eight steps.
The three disciplines—tapas or auste-rity, स्वाध्याय or study of the scriptures as also the जप of प्रणव (Om) and ईश्वरप्रणिधान (surrendering the fruits of actions to God)—together form kriyā-योग. They are called ‘kriyāyoga’ since they are in the form of kriyā (activity) and lead to योग (union with God) in course of time.
Tapas or austerity consists of physical austerity like serving the elders and continence, austerity of speech like speaking the truth and the study of the वेदस्, and, austerity of मिन्द् like purity of emotions.
Svādhyāya includes the study of scriptures that help in the path towards कैवल्य (liberation) and the repetition of mantras like Om and the गायत्री.
Īśvarapraṇidhāna comprises offering all actions and their fruits at the feet of God.
This क्रियायोग helps in the attenuation of evil qualities and ultimately leads to समाधि.
